title: Tale of the Jewish Doctor

full_text:
To entertain the Sultan of China and clear his own name in the strange affair of the hunchback, the Jewish physician related a mystery from his youth in Damascus:

"In my early years of practice, I was summoned in haste to the palace of the city governor to treat a young merchant of Baghdad who had fallen into a deep swoon. When I loosened his garments, I discovered that his right wrist had been severed and wrapped in scented silk bandages. After reviving him with cordials and smelling salts, I sat beside his couch, struck by his noble countenance and sorrowful eyes.

Seeing my genuine concern, the young merchant wept and confided his secret: 'Know, O doctor, that I was once wealthy, inheriting a grand silk emporium. While trading in Damascus, a veiled lady of matchless beauty entered my shop, purchasing costly brocades on credit. For weeks she returned, always paying with purest gold dinars and speaking with refined grace. My heart became deeply attached to her virtues.'

One evening, she invited him to her family's garden mansion. As they sat dining beneath jasmine arbors, a precious golden necklace belonging to the governor's household went missing from the terrace. The household guards surrounded the garden, and in the confusion, the young merchant, wishing to shield the maiden from disgrace, placed the jewel in his own pocket, intending to return it to the governor at dawn.

The guards searched him, discovered the necklace, and dragged him before the magistrate as a thief. The harsh magistrate ordered his hand severed according to the strict law of the city. Only later did the governor's wife confess that her pet monkey had snatched the necklace and dropped it upon the garden path.

The remorseful governor bestowed palaces, wealth, and the maiden's hand upon the noble youth to atone for the error. 'I bear this severed hand,' concluded the merchant, 'as a testament to the peril of hasty judgment.' I attended to his wound with all my skill, marveling at how noble souls bear adversity with silent dignity."
moral: Honest compassion and professional duty bridge all divides, while hasty suspicion brings regret.
